currentRead.verdict: Constructive, but only if AWS AI capex converts into reaccelerating high-margin cloud growth and advertising continues to fund retail reinvestment.
currentRead.variantView: The core debate has moved from simple retail margin recovery to whether Amazon can run three compounding engines at once: AWS AI, retail media advertising, and fulfillment efficiency, without permanently impairing normalized free cash flow.
currentRead.marketIsWatching: AWS AI demand and Trainium adoption, AI capex/FCF drag, advertising growth and Prime Video ads, North America retail margin, International profit inflection, Project Kuiper dilution, and FTC/EU marketplace risk.
currentRead.valuationGuardrail: Do not underwrite AMZN from current price or current multiple. Stress AWS growth, AWS margin, ad growth, normalized FCF margin, and capex intensity independently.

themeTiles.title: AWS AI Demand and Custom Silicon
themeTiles.marketFocus: Investors are watching whether Bedrock, Amazon Q, Anthropic demand, Trainium, Inferentia, and GPU capacity translate into AWS reacceleration.
themeTiles.evidence: AWS is still the highest-quality profit engine, but AI infrastructure intensity raises the hurdle rate for every incremental dollar of growth.
themeTiles.modelDriver: AWS revenue growth, AWS operating margin, AWS revenue multiple, and AI capex drag.
themeTiles.bullCase: Trainium and Bedrock improve cost-to-serve, AWS growth reaccelerates, and margins hold despite depreciation.
themeTiles.bearCase: AI workloads are price-competitive, GPU depreciation rises, and AWS growth does not justify capex.

themeTiles.title: AI Capex Versus Normalized FCF
themeTiles.marketFocus: The stock can look expensive or cheap depending on whether AI capex is temporary growth investment or a structurally higher maintenance burden.
themeTiles.evidence: Reported FCF is the wrong single number if growth capex is mixed with maintenance capex, but normalized FCF should not add back every dollar of AI spend.
themeTiles.modelDriver: Capex intensity, maintenance capex intensity, normalized FCF margin, discount rate, and target FCF yield.
themeTiles.bullCase: Growth capex creates durable cloud capacity and retail logistics leverage, allowing normalized FCF to expand after the buildout.
themeTiles.bearCase: AI capacity becomes a recurring arms race and normalized FCF remains structurally below consensus.

themeTiles.title: Advertising and Prime Video Ads
themeTiles.marketFocus: Advertising is increasingly treated as a separate high-margin profit pool inside the retail traffic graph.
themeTiles.evidence: Retail media, sponsored ads, and Prime Video ads can fund fulfillment, content, and price investment if growth remains resilient.
themeTiles.modelDriver: Advertising revenue growth, contribution margin, advertising revenue multiple, and subscription flywheel durability.
themeTiles.bullCase: Ads keep compounding above retail growth and Prime Video ads add high-quality inventory without hurting retention.
themeTiles.bearCase: Ad load, measurement quality, or competition slows ad growth and multiple support fades.

themeTiles.title: North America Retail Margin Durability
themeTiles.marketFocus: After the post-pandemic cost reset, the key question is whether fulfillment regionalization and delivery density continue to lift margins.
themeTiles.evidence: Retail operating leverage matters because small margin changes on North America revenue move consolidated EBIT materially.
themeTiles.modelDriver: North America operating margin, shipping cost, fulfillment cost, and third-party seller services mix.
themeTiles.bullCase: Regionalization, automation, and ad-funded retail traffic support a higher through-cycle margin.
themeTiles.bearCase: Labor, fuel, last-mile intensity, and low-price competitors re-pressure retail profitability.

themeTiles.title: International Profit Inflection
themeTiles.marketFocus: International profitability is a swing factor: it can become an EBIT contributor or a reinvestment sink.
themeTiles.evidence: The model treats International margin as a separate driver because the revenue base is large and operating leverage is uneven by region.
themeTiles.modelDriver: International growth, International operating margin, FX, and retail EBIT multiple.
themeTiles.bullCase: Mature markets scale, emerging markets remain disciplined, and FX does not reverse operating leverage.
themeTiles.bearCase: Competition and reinvestment push International back toward losses.

themeTiles.title: Project Kuiper, Zoox, and Long-Duration Options
themeTiles.marketFocus: Kuiper and other options can be strategically valuable, but only if they do not mask core FCF dilution.
themeTiles.evidence: The research framework gives options explicit value, with bear-case zero value and separate capex/ROIC monitoring.
themeTiles.modelDriver: Kuiper option value, AI capex drag, normalized FCF margin, and risk premium.
themeTiles.bullCase: Kuiper supports connectivity, cloud edge, and ecosystem leverage beyond current retail/cloud economics.
themeTiles.bearCase: Capital intensity rises before commercial proof and investors discount the option to zero.

themeTiles.title: Regulation, Marketplace Fees, and Labor
themeTiles.marketFocus: The risk debate is whether regulation hits only merchant economics or Amazon's own fee, ad, and fulfillment profit pools.
themeTiles.evidence: Marketplace, ad ranking, seller fees, Prime, data usage, labor, and EU/FTC actions can affect both margin and multiple.
themeTiles.modelDriver: Retail EBIT multiple, advertising contribution margin, discount rate, and normalized FCF margin.
themeTiles.bullCase: Regulation remains manageable and does not impair traffic, fee take-rate, or ad inventory.
themeTiles.bearCase: Fee limits, ranking transparency, labor cost, or antitrust remedies compress profit-pool durability.

killCriteria: AWS growth fails to reaccelerate while capex intensity remains high.
AWS margin compresses for several quarters without evidence of better utilization.
Advertising growth falls toward consolidated retail growth and loses premium-multiple status.
North America retail margin stalls while shipping and fulfillment cost intensity rises.
International profit inflection reverses into recurring losses.
Kuiper or other long-duration options absorb capital without commercial proof.
Regulatory remedies materially reduce marketplace fees, ad ranking flexibility, or seller economics.
monitoringPlan: Track AWS growth, AWS margin, and AI capex intensity every quarter.
Track advertising revenue growth versus consolidated revenue growth.
Track North America and International operating income separately.
Track reported FCF versus normalized FCF, including leases and growth capex treatment.
Track Prime/subscription revenue as evidence of retention and ad-inventory quality.
Track Kuiper launch and customer proof points before assigning option value.
